I originally purchased the Whirlpool replacement filters, but the cheaper alternatives were no longer available on Amazon. As these came in at a fraction of the cost and had somewhat good reviews I decided to give them a try. The filter, while it does work, is definitely different. First, the top part that slides into the handle is a lot smaller than the original, which means it slides around a lot. Not a deal breaker, but definitely different. Second, the twist connections on the tip are in a different location. Meaning, with the original filter I would put the filter in with the handle in the 12 o'clock position, then I would twist over to the arrow to the 3 o'clock position. With this one, I put it in with the handle at the 10 o'clock position, and stop at the 1 o'clock position. Again, not a deal breaker. Just annoying as it doesn't line up with the refrigerators built in arrows which would make one thing it's not screwed all the way in. Lastly, and this is the most annoying, is this filter is LOUD. I could always hear the water through the other filters when they were new before they were purged, but this one is consistently loud. So much so that I thought I didn't have it screwed in all the way. Going to go back to Whirlpool's filters, or look for a different alternative

Like most I was disappointed when the reusable pod didn't unlock the additional sizes.  But not to be deterred I took a hack used to fool the keurig into unlocking the additional sizes and applied it to this guy and voilà! My 14 oz is back.  Basically just take a used or unwanted carafe pod, cut off the green dot, and tape it to the red dot on the pod. Not sure if a green sticker will work as well as I didn't have one, but based on the pictures, this for sure works and it brews 14 oz just fine.  Although the size will be available with this hack, the pod is not able to hold enough grounds to brew a carafe.  4 stars because yes it works like it's supposed to, but it's something that should have been included with the unit in the first place.
